rationale: THE `renders` FIXTURE — a component RENDERS another component, and the REFUSALS around it. THE CONTRACT (`src/ast/types.ts:131-140`): source = the rendering symbol, target = the rendered component. The fleet's other lanes publish it in this shape — typescript/javascript: the enclosing component function -> the JSX tag name; clojure: the enclosing fn -> the component symbol inside a hiccup vector; csharp: the rendering context -> the component named by a type argument. DART'S CONSTRUCT IS FLUTTER'S `build` METHOD: `class Home extends StatelessWidget { Widget build(BuildContext context) => Scaffold(); }` — `Home` IS the component and `Scaffold` IS the component it renders, the structural analogue of a React component returning `<Scaffold/>`. Dart has no JSX, so the syntax that carries the construct is the rendering ENTRY POINT, and NO GRAMMAR CHANGE is needed: the existing `method_signature`, `function_body`, `const_object_expression`, `new_expression` and `identifier`+`selector` node types carry it (R3). This fixture pins TWO things. POSITIVE: all FOUR of dart's construction spellings publish the SAME edge — the modern call `Scaffold()`, the const construction `const Scaffold()`, the `new` construction `new Scaffold()` and the block body `return Scaffold();` — because a lane that handled only one of them would pass one row and fail the other three. NEGATIVE: the refused shapes publish NO render row. The negative half is the half a prose claim cannot fake: an analyzer that published a render for EVERY construction inside a build method, or for a build method that returns a variable, or for a lowercase name, would pass every positive row in this file and fail these. The named refusals are: (1) NotReturned — the construction is NOT the returned expression, so it stays an `instantiates` row and no render is published; (2) ReturnsVariable — the build method returns a variable, so no component is NAMED; (3) ReturnsCall — it returns a call to a helper, so no component is NAMED; (4) NotAWidget — the declared return type is not `Widget`, so it is not a rendering host; (5) Lowercase — a lowercase name is not a class (dart's own naming convention, the same test the JS lane applies to a JSX tag, where `<div>` is an intrinsic and not a component). The population behind both halves is measured over the whole admitted corpus by `script/m14/dart-extended-constructs.ts` (the `renders` section of `validation/m14/measurements/dart-extended-constructs-2026-10-21.json`).

expectRelationships.note: POSITIVE 1 — THE MODERN CALL. `Widget build(BuildContext context) => Scaffold();` — the dart grammar spells this construction as a BARE `identifier` FOLLOWED BY A `selector` (the call), so a lane that only read `const_object_expression` would miss it. The source is the COMPONENT (the class), not the method, exactly as the JS lane's source is the enclosing component function.

POSITIVE 2 — THE CONST CONSTRUCTION. `=> const Scaffold();` is a `const_object_expression`; the component name is its `type_identifier` child, NOT the `const_builtin` keyword and NOT the argument list.

POSITIVE 3 — THE `new` CONSTRUCTION. `=> new Scaffold();` is a `new_expression`. Dart has no `new` in practice, but the grammar carries it and the row must not depend on which spelling the source used.

POSITIVE 4 — THE BLOCK BODY. `{ return Scaffold(); }` — the returned expression is the `return_statement`'s own expression, one level deeper than the arrow body. A lane that read only the arrow form would pass the other three and fail this.

POSITIVE 5 — THE ORDINARY ROW IS NOT SWALLOWED. The construction in `NotReturned` is not the returned expression, so it stays an `instantiates` row: the render row is an ADDITIONAL fact about the widget tree, not a replacement of the call/instantiation row.

forbidRelationships.note: REFUSAL 1 — THE CONSTRUCTION IS NOT THE RETURNED EXPRESSION. `Scaffold();` on its own line is a construction, but the build method returns `_cached`, so no component is rendered: the render row must be read off the RETURNED expression only.
REFUSAL 2 — THE BUILD METHOD RETURNS A VARIABLE. `=> _cached!;` names no component, so there is nothing to render; the nearest construct is a value read and it stays a `uses` row.

REFUSAL 3 — THE BUILD METHOD RETURNS A CALL. `=> _helper();` names no component either; the helper call stays a `calls` row. A lane that treated every call in a build method as a render would publish a row here.

REFUSAL 4 — NOT A RENDERING HOST. `int build() => 1;` — the declared return type is not `Widget`, so the method is not Flutter's rendering entry point. Without the return-type test, ANY class with a `build()` method would qualify, including the protobuf-style message builders whose `build()` returns a message and not a component.

REFUSAL 5 — A LOWERCASE NAME IS NOT A CLASS. dart's own naming convention, the same test the JS lane applies to a JSX tag (`<div>` is an intrinsic, not a component). The lowercase call stays a `calls` row.

THE SUPERCLASS IS NOT WHAT IS RENDERED. `extends StatelessWidget` is an `extends` row; the rendered component is the one the build method RETURNS. A lane that published the superclass as the rendered component would pass every positive row above and still be wrong.

THE SOURCE IS THE COMPONENT, NOT THE METHOD. Every render row's source is the class that renders; a row whose source is the bare method name `build` would be ambiguous across every widget in the file — and this file has SEVEN classes with a `build` method, which is what makes the check falsifiable rather than cosmetic.
